stemBlocks.value: Think first: No pair of whole numbers multiplies to −4 and adds to 6, so this one needs the formula or completing the square.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write down a, b and c.
Simplify by dividing through by 2 and evaluate.

strategyBlocks.value: Identify a, b and c, substitute into the quadratic formula, then simplify the surd and give decimal values.

whyThisWorks.value: The quadratic formula is completing the square carried out once and for all on ax² + bx + c = 0, so it always works, factorisable or not. The discriminant 52 is positive but not a perfect square, which is precisely why no whole-number factorisation exists and the roots are irrational. Simplifying √52 to 2√13 lets the 2 cancel with the denominator, giving the neat exact form −3 ± √13.

commonErrors.misconception: Taking c as +4 and getting a discriminant of 20.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Taking c as +4 and getting a discriminant of 20.

commonErrors.misconception: Dividing only the surd by 2 and leaving −6 undivided.

examTip.value: Compute the discriminant on its own line first — it tells you straight away whether nice factors exist and guards against sign errors.
